H1.statement: Crack spread futures are the most significant predictors of downstream financial performance.
H1.evidence: CRACK_SPREAD_MA_5 (71.81% importance) and CRACK_SPREAD_LAG_1 (27.19% importance) are the top two features in Random Forest. Both models show >77.0% R² using these features.
H1.statistical_support: Feature importance > 99.0% combined for top 2 features

H2.statement: Ensemble machine learning models (XGBoost, Random Forest) will significantly outperform traditional time-series models (ARIMA) in forecasting crack spreads.
H2.evidence: Random Forest RMSE = 17.42 vs ARIMA RMSE = 48.35 (64.0% improvement). Random Forest R² = 0.770 vs ARIMA R² = -0.769.

H3.statement: Crude oil volatility significantly moderates forecasting accuracy.
H3.evidence: Volatility features in top 10 positions (0.10-0.31% importance). Models capture volatility through multiple features.
H3.statistical_support: Feature importance: Volatility features <0.31% but consistently present

H4.statement: Incorporating refinery utilization and inventory data improves forecast accuracy.
H4.evidence: Multi-feature approach achieved R² = 0.770 with 36 features across multiple categories.
